title: Graph evaluation is injective for equivariant locally constant functions
statement: Let $V$ be a scheme, $P$ a finite group, $c:Y\to V$ a finite etale $\operatorname{ULift}(P)$-torsor [def-sbc-normal-dominant-galois], $\ell\in\mathbb N$, and $N$ a $P$-representation over $\mathbb Z/\ell$. Let $W$ be an etale $V$-object and $f:W\to Y$ a morphism over $V$. The equivariant locally constant functions $s:W\times_VY\to N$ are defined in [def-weil-pbc-torsor-associated-module], with $s(gx)=\rho(g)s(x)$. Restriction of these functions along the graph $j_f=(\mathrm{id}_W,f)$ is injective. The torsor site object is as in [def-weil-pbc-torsor-section-representation]. No connectedness or primality assumption is required.

proof.text: Swap the two projections in the defining torsor isomorphism to obtain the splitting with components (id,smul g). Base change along f using the already proved CategoryTheory.FinitaryPreExtensive.isIso_sigmaDesc_lift_comp, and identify the pullback along f followed by c with the pullback along W.hom. Its g-th component is the graph followed by sectionAction g. An isomorphism of schemes is surjective on points, and the sigma open cover therefore makes these components jointly surjective.

For two equivariant functions with the same graph restriction, express any point as sectionAction g applied to a graph point. Equivariance makes both values rho(g) applied to the common graph value. Pointwise extensionality then proves equality of the functions and subtype extensionality proves equality of the equivariant sections. Empty W gives vacuous pointwise equality.

lean.statement:
theorem graphEvaluation_injective
    {V : Scheme.{u}} (ℓ : ℕ) {P : Type u} [Group P] [Finite P]
    (c : Scheme.GaloisCover (ULift.{u + 1} P) V)
    (N : Rep.{u + 1} (ZMod ℓ) P) (W : V.Etale)
    (f : W ⟶ c.sectionObject) :
    Function.Injective (fun s : c.equivariantSections ℓ N W ↦
      LocallyConstant.comap
        (pullback.lift (f := W.hom) (g := c.π) (𝟙 W.left) f.left
          (by simpa using (MorphismProperty.Over.w f).symm)).base.hom s.val)
